chapter: Central Avenue, WPA and the Alabam era
title: Dunbar Hotel, the Last Word and Alton Redd
summary: They discuss the Club Alabam beside the Dunbar Hotel, the Last Word, and Redd's father Alton hiring musicians.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Can you remember the names of any of the clubs other than the Club Alabam, which was adjacent to the Dunbar Hotel, which is now a historical monument-- historical landmark, in Los Angeles. This is the hotel that was owned by Dr. Summerville, the black dentist.
The black entertainers and musicians could not live in downtown Los Angeles at this time. Was there the Last Word? That was there too.
Your dad can remember all that now. I can see him.
Yes, he was very active in that time. He hired quite a few musicians during the time.
Leonard Davidson, "Big Boy", was with him during this time thereabout and he continued to do so throughout this period until about World War II, when the whole scene started to branch out a bit more.
